messages:
mike: Heads up — we saw a burst of fncall schema rejects on eu-west this morning tied to route_id=kp-translate. Customers saw 5xxs. sample traces attached in logs.
anya: ugh, what's the reject shape? full payload or just extra fields?
ryan: quick glance: model returned an extra top-level field `confidence` alongside the expected {result:string, tools:[]}, so strict validator treats as invalid_shape.
mike: exact snippet from the response that failed validation (redacted customer data):
```json
{
  "result": "translated text",
  "tools": [],
  "confidence": 0.92
}
```
kelly: that extra field shouldn't be fatal in permissive mode. Is the route using strict validate=true?
mike: yes, kp-translate had strict validation after the canary. Canary was at 20% yesterday and it flipped to 100% at 02:13 UTC.
anya: can we see telemetry tags? want to know if billing/quota attribution is correct for those rejects.
ops-bot: fncall.validate.reject count=47 route_id=kp-translate region=eu-west severity=hard code=invalid_shape validation_version=v2 sample_rate=0.01
ryan: looks like we only sampled 1% of payloads, which is why SRE got noisy alerts but no payloads in console.
kelly: console UX ask: add a column for `reject_mode` (strict|permissive) + ability to link to a sampled payload even when sample_rate low. Right now it just shows counts.
mike: agree. Also need a clear distinction in dashboards: hard rejects (error returned to customer) vs soft-log (accepted but flagged). Right now both increment the same metric.
anya: proposal: split metrics into fncall.rejects.hard and fncall.rejects.soft; keep fncall.rejects.total for compatibility. Add labels: validation_version, rule_id, route_id.
ryan: Implementation note: splitting metrics will inflate cardinality. We should only attach rule_id and validation_version for sampled events, keep counts aggregated by (route,region,severity).
kelly: acceptable. For console, surface the sample link when any sample exists; allow on-demand sampling: a developer button that requests an additional sample from warm logs for last 5m (consent only).
mike: on-demand sampling is nice but we need privacy guardrails — must redact PII and check tenant settings. Also cost/retention implications.
anya: telemetry change: attach a compact rejection signature to every reject (sha256 of sorted keys + reason) so we can group without storing whole payloads. That keeps cardinality low.
ryan: +1. We can store signature as label and only store raw payloads when sample hit or on-demand export.
kelly: rollout plan? we should not flip strict validators to permissive automatically. Do a reversible canary: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with a 24h observation window, plus a metric guard: if hard rejects drop less than 80% or user error rate increases, rollback.
mike: propose an interim quick patch: for kp-translate, revert strict->permissive until we ship the UI changes. Can ops revert?
ops-bot: Revert trigger accepted. Rolling back validation config for route_id=kp-translate to previous (permissive) at 1768456825.
anya: once reverted, we'll prepare the dashboard changes: new columns (reject_mode, signature, sample_link) and split metrics. I'll draft a schema for the new telemetry fields.
ryan: draft schema suggestion (compact):
```
fncall.reject.event {
  route_id: string,
  region: string,
  severity: enum(hard,soft),
  signature: string,        # sha256(keys+reason)
  validation_version: string,
  rule_id: string?,
  trace_id: string?,
}
```
kelly: looks good. For console listing, show top 5 signatures for a route last 24h and a quick view of example fields that differ.
mike: one more ask: attribution for quota/billing — do rejects count against token billing? we need to confirm. If strict validators are rejecting before billing, customers are getting 5xx and might not be charged but it still impacts UX.
ryan: current pipeline charges on successful token completion. Hard rejects returned before cost-incurring step should not bill tokens. We need to add metric fncall.rejects.billable=true/false to be certain.
anya: I'll add billable label to the telemetry schema. Also will add validation_version so we can backfill issues to a specific validator rollout.
kelly: OK. Next actions: Anya to PR telemetry + console wireframe, Ryan to implement signature generator & metric split, Ops to confirm rollback is stable and watch alerts, Mike to notify CS about temporary revert.
mike: thanks — ping me once PRs land. I'll coordinate a small postmortem to capture the canary flip that caused this.
ops-bot: Note: rollback completed and alerts suppressed for route_id=kp-translate at 1768456826.
anya: filing PRs now, linking to this thread.
ryan: will prototype grouping logic and a low-cardinality retention strategy.
kelly: I'll mock up console column layout and a sample-redaction plan.
mike: dropping a short postmortem draft after we have metrics. Done for now.
